results.evidence: normalize_query_for_write now has `if existing_uuid: ... else: normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())`, so a supplied uuid is discarded on create; the rest of the query is copied via dict(query).
update_saved_metric passes existing_uuid; `if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid` preserves it.

For each of ("metrics","metrics_secondary") not in update_data, if any stored metric's uuid is in attached_saved_metric_uuids, `update_data[metric_field] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(stored_metrics, seen=seen_metric_uuids)`. seen contains the attached uuids, so the clashing metric is regenerated. Depends on the unseen _assign_uuids_to_metrics regenerating duplicates against seen.

The rewrite only happens inside the `if any(... in attached_saved_metric_uuids ...)` guard. Without a clash update_data is not touched for that field, so the stored metrics and ordering stay unchanged.

The rewrite runs before _sync_ordering_with_metric_changes. The existing comment says regenerated dups keep the original uuid in ordering and the new uuid is appended, and _sync_ordering_for_saved_metrics_on_update covers the shared uuid. I could not see the ordering sync code itself, so this rests on that comment.
The new block only writes update_data for inline metric fields. Saved metric rows and the link sync code are untouched, and the uuid set is only read.

The guidance now says to create the shared metric "with the same `query`" and send one update that attaches it and resends `metrics` without the inline copy. It never tells the agent to omit the identifier (uuid) when creating the shared metric, so half of the required instruction is missing.

When metrics is resent, seen_metric_uuids already includes the linked saved metric uuids (from the current links in the else branch, or from the payload). `_assign_uuids_to_metrics(update_data["metrics"], seen=seen_metric_uuids)` regenerates the clashing inline uuid. This is unchanged pre-existing behavior.
